newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to effectively bar personal fund trading - paper.
newsitem.headline: HK to effectively bar personal fund trading - paper.

text.p: The Hong Kong Investment Funds Association (HKIFA) has proposed guidelines to effectively bar speculative personal account dealing by fund managers, the South China Morning Post reported on Friday.

The Securities and Futures Commission and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong were reviewing a draft report compiled by the HKIFA which would apply to all employees of HKIFA members and cover transactions of spouses and immediate family members, it said.
Procedures for holding personal accounts would be made onerous enough to discourage most employees from considering personal dealing, the newspaper cited a leaked copy of the report as saying.
HKIFA officials were not immediately available for comment.
The proposals were made in the wake of widespread industry concern following a recent trading scandal at Jardine Fleming.

Regulators hit the company with a stiff fine and withdrew the authorisation of its London-based fund arm in September following revelations of late allocation of trades by a senior fund manager. Many of the trades involved his personal account.
The proposed HKIFA guidelines were an attempt to provide minimum standards for best practices in the industry without imposing onerous practices on fund managers and firms, the Morning Post said.
It was the first time the association has moved to draw together the various regulations and guidelines concerning the primacy of client interests, the newspaper said.
